mostWorthwhile.text: Making a specific spring-tide prediction and checking it at the shore was most worthwhile: it turned a mythic connection into an observation that could challenge an explanation, while acknowledging local variation and the limits of agreement.

leastWorthwhile.text: The repeated empty compatibility lists made the early route frustrating and unclear, especially after plausible attempts to connect curiosity and observation.

surprise.text: Wonder had no available combinations when I first tried it, but later became useful after language was created. That changed my understanding of how the chapter unlocks its ideas.

arbitrary.text: The need to make a calendar before the lunar hypothesis could be tested felt under-signposted: the direct shore attempt failed even though the shore seemed like the natural place to observe tides.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see where shared discovery leads, particularly if another chapter offers similarly concrete tests with a clearer route through its combinations.
